status: proposed; unresolved user scope recorded in open-questions.md

categories.name: Falcone contracts and developer experience
categories.goal: Preserve Falcone-facing behavior and establish the exact replacement boundary.

stories.title: Inventory and freeze the Falcone workflow contracts
stories.story: As a Falcone maintainer, I want a versioned contract inventory so that replacement cannot silently change existing behavior.
stories.description: Inventory routes, DSL, errors, roles, schedules, monitoring and task envelopes against pinned source and deployed fixtures.
requirements: The system must preserve inventoried Falcone workflow API routes, response schemas, status codes and tenant-scoped identifiers through a compatibility facade.
The project must publish a compatibility matrix marking each observed behavior as preserved, intentionally versioned, or a migration blocker.
acceptance: Capture fixtures for definition CRUD, publish, validate, executions, cancel, retry, signal, catalog and schedules.
Include existing SSE node-status/log-line/stream-end frames and Last-Event-ID behavior.
Record whether arbitrary Temporal SDK workflows exist; do not claim raw SDK compatibility without evidence.

stories.title: Implement the Falcone facade and backend routing
stories.story: As an application developer, I want stable Falcone APIs so that clients survive the engine migration.
stories.description: Introduce a narrow WorkflowBackend interface inside Falcone; separate public compatibility from internal engine routes.
requirements: The system must expose authenticated start, get, list, cancel, retry and signal operations with tenant-scoped idempotency keys.
The system must route every existing run to its recorded backend and return a retryable service-unavailable response when that backend is unavailable.
acceptance: Concurrent identical starts yield one run; reuse of the key with different input returns a conflict.
Historic Temporal runs remain queryable and cancellable during mixed operation.
Connection failure followed by recovery succeeds without process restart; legacy error mappings are fixture-tested.

stories.title: Provide CLI and console integration contracts
stories.story: As a Falcone user, I want familiar authoring and monitoring tools so that I do not need another workflow portal.
stories.description: Use the current console DSL and task catalog; add CLI operations through the same facade.
requirements: The system must support CLI validate, publish, start, inspect, cancel and retry operations using Falcone authentication.
The system must provide versioned task schemas and validation errors usable by Falcone's existing visual editor.
acceptance: CLI and console send equivalent requests and display stable error codes.
A round-trip through the editor preserves all supported DSL fields.
Read-only users can inspect authorized flows but cannot publish definitions.

categories.name: DSL interpretation and versioning
categories.goal: Build a native interpreter for Falcone definitions without executing arbitrary tenant orchestration code.

stories.title: Qualify and compile the existing Falcone DSL
stories.story: As a flow author, I want my current definitions to work so that migration does not require rewriting every flow.
stories.description: Compile v1.0 graph structure to an immutable execution plan; preserve schema and validator diagnostics.
requirements: The system must validate sequence, parallel, task, branch, wait, approval and sub-flow nodes using the inventoried Falcone DSL rules.
The system must reject invalid cycles, duplicate IDs, unknown tasks, dangling references and invalid cron/duration expressions before publishing.
acceptance: All existing valid and invalid DSL fixtures produce equivalent results or documented blockers.
Compilation stores schema version, plan hash and interpreter version.
Repeated node references receive unique execution occurrence IDs while retaining canvas node IDs.

stories.title: Implement bounded expressions and graph semantics
stories.story: As a flow author, I want predictable branches and parallel joins so that failures do not change business outcomes.
stories.description: Keep CEL semantics compatible with existing fixtures; isolate evaluation and persist selected branches and outputs.
requirements: The system must evaluate expressions with bounded input size, runtime and memory without network, filesystem or arbitrary-code access.
The system must persist branch decisions, parallel completion sets and deterministic output-merge behavior before advancing successors.
acceptance: CEL compatibility fixtures cover nulls, numbers, errors and time-sensitive inputs; incompatible expressions block migration.
Crash/restart at a branch or join neither duplicates successors nor loses completed branches.
Conflicting parallel writes are rejected or resolved by a versioned documented rule; elapsed time is not an implicit merge order.

stories.title: Pin definitions, children and interpreter semantics
stories.story: As an operator, I want safe upgrades so that long-running flows retain their intended behavior.
stories.description: Version definitions, connector contracts and interpreter semantics independently; retain old interpreters while runs drain.
requirements: The system must pin each run to immutable definition and interpreter versions and each child to an authorized explicit definition version.
The system must reject unsupported historical versions and require an explicit audited migration plan before changing active-run semantics.
acceptance: Publishing a new definition leaves active parent and child runs unchanged.
A rolling upgrade with old/new evaluators completes compatible runs and leaves unsupported runs safely parked.
Bounded sub-flow depth and expanded graph size prevent recursive resource exhaustion.

categories.name: Durable state and recovery
categories.goal: Make PostgreSQL transactions the authoritative boundary for workflow progress.

stories.title: Implement the transactional run state machine
stories.story: As a platform engineer, I want atomic state transitions so that crashes cannot lose accepted work.
stories.description: Persist run state, history, ready work and outbox records in one transaction with optimistic revisions.
requirements: The system must acknowledge a start only after committing the run, pinned plan, first ready work, audit event and idempotency record.
The system must commit each state transition, ordered per-run event and generated work atomically under a checked revision.
acceptance: Fault injection before/after commit proves that acknowledged starts remain discoverable.
Two evaluators racing one revision produce exactly one committed transition.
No production in-memory fallback exists when PostgreSQL is unavailable.

stories.title: Add task leases, fencing and recovery scans
stories.story: As an SRE, I want workers to recover abandoned tasks so that node failure does not strand runs.
stories.description: Claim ready tasks with bounded leases, database time, monotonic attempt fencing and periodic reconciliation.
requirements: The system must reject task completions and heartbeats with expired or superseded lease generations.
The system must recover abandoned tasks through durable scans even when all optional notifications are lost.
acceptance: Kill a worker after claim and verify another claims after expiry.
An old worker completion cannot change a newer attempt or terminal run.
DB disconnection stops new dispatch; bounded reconnection resumes scanning without manual repair.

stories.title: Bound history and verify disaster recovery
stories.story: As an operator, I want recoverable compact state so that months-long runs do not create unbounded replay costs.
stories.description: Use explicit continuations and snapshots; preserve audit order and payload references through archival.
requirements: The system must bound event history and payload growth using configured limits and resumable continuation or archival policies.
The system must restore database and referenced object payloads to a consistent recovery point and reconcile external effects before resuming dispatch.
acceptance: Restore an encrypted backup into an isolated environment and complete waiting and running fixtures.
Compacted runs retain a contiguous inspectable event lineage or an explicit archive cursor.
Recovery reports possible post-backup external effects and prevents automatic duplicate dispatch until reconciled.

categories.name: Task execution and long-running work
categories.goal: Separate orchestration from side effects and enforce honest delivery semantics.

stories.title: Define the native activity worker protocol
stories.story: As a connector maintainer, I want an engine-neutral task context so that Falcone adapters no longer import Temporal.
stories.description: Specify claim, heartbeat, complete and fail messages with run/occurrence/attempt identity and credentials.
requirements: The system must dispatch tasks through a versioned protocol carrying tenant, workspace, run, node occurrence, attempt, lease generation and pinned adapter version.
The system must execute side effects only in authorized workers and must reject unknown task types in production.
acceptance: A native worker executes a test connector without any Temporal SDK import.
Invalid tenant, adapter version or lease metadata is rejected before connector I/O.
Production dispatch cannot reach the legacy echo/mock fallback.

stories.title: Implement retries, deadlines and side-effect safety
stories.story: As a workflow author, I want controlled retries so that transient failures recover without uncontrolled duplicate effects.
stories.description: Use stable business-operation idempotency keys across attempts, typed errors and durable retry timers.
requirements: The system must apply configured maximum attempts, backoff, retryable error classes, start-to-close, schedule-to-close and heartbeat timeouts.
The system must classify connectors by idempotency support and surface ambiguous external outcomes instead of promising universal exactly-once effects.
acceptance: Inject a crash after external success but before completion commit; idempotent connector deduplicates the retry.
Non-idempotent connector enters reconciliation-required when success is ambiguous.
Run cancellation and retry budgets terminate new attempts without erasing prior outcomes.

stories.title: Support asynchronous jobs and checkpoints
stories.story: As a data analyst, I want long-running tasks to survive worker restarts so that analysis is resumable.
stories.description: Separate job submission, observation, checkpoint and result retrieval; avoid holding orchestration processes during waits.
requirements: The system must persist external job IDs and checkpoint references and resume observation after worker loss without blindly resubmitting the job.
The system must support configurable multi-day waits with bounded heartbeat, cancellation and credential-renewal policies.
acceptance: A worker dies after job submission; reconciliation finds the same external job.
A cancelled job cannot report the workflow completed; delayed cleanup is visible and retried under policy.
A capability-qualified checkpoint resumes correctly; unsupported native workloads remain migration blockers.

categories.name: Timers and schedules
categories.goal: Replace Temporal timers and schedules with durable Falcone-owned scheduling.

stories.title: Implement durable timers and race resolution
stories.story: As a workflow author, I want durable delays so that waits survive outages.
stories.description: Store due timestamps in PostgreSQL, use database time and serialize timer firing with signals/cancellation.
requirements: The system must persist wait and retry timers and fire each logical timer at most once into workflow state.
The system must resolve simultaneous signal, timeout and cancellation transitions with one documented transactional ordering rule.
acceptance: Restart all engine pods while a timer is pending; it fires after recovery.
Race an approval, timeout and cancellation and verify one accepted outcome and audited losers.
Clock skew between workers does not move a database-timed deadline earlier.

stories.title: Replace flow schedules with compatible controls
stories.story: As a workspace owner, I want existing cron controls so that scheduled automation remains operable.
stories.description: Preserve one schedule per flow and public list/get/pause/resume/trigger responses; persist occurrence identity.
requirements: The system must preserve Falcone schedule identities, published cron text, next-action times, recent actions and idempotent pause/resume behavior.
The system must implement explicit overlap, catch-up window, timezone and daylight-saving policies and atomically deduplicate each scheduled occurrence.
acceptance: Fixtures match the current schedule API, including absent and foreign schedules.
Concurrent schedulers create one run per occurrence and enforce overlap policy.
DST transitions and outage catch-up produce documented bounded outcomes.

stories.title: Coordinate schedule cutover and backfill
stories.story: As an operator, I want one active schedule owner so that migration cannot double-fire workflows.
stories.description: Add backend ownership epochs, bounded backfill and reconciliation against legacy schedule state.
requirements: The system must fence schedule ownership during backend handover so only one engine may admit an occurrence.
The system must support audited bounded backfill with a preview of candidate occurrences and quota impact.
acceptance: Pause legacy admission, reconcile accepted occurrences, transfer the ownership epoch and resume the new scheduler.
A stale schedule owner cannot admit runs after handover.
Backfill cancellation stops future admissions without deleting already accepted runs.

categories.name: Events and trigger delivery
categories.goal: Use Falcone's existing event infrastructure with durable inbox/outbox semantics.

stories.title: Add inbox and outbox integration
stories.story: As a platform engineer, I want durable event delivery so that broker outages cannot lose workflow transitions.
stories.description: Use Kafka as transport, PostgreSQL as state authority; enforce tenant-bound event identities.
requirements: The system must persist incoming trigger/event deduplication records and resulting workflow transitions before acknowledging delivery.
The system must publish committed outgoing events through a retryable transactional outbox with stable event IDs.
acceptance: Crash between DB commit and broker acknowledgement; redelivery causes no second logical admission.
Crash after publish but before outbox acknowledgement; consumer deduplication handles repeat delivery.
Broker unavailability accumulates bounded backlog and exposes age/size metrics.

stories.title: Preserve webhook and platform-event triggers
stories.story: As a Falcone user, I want existing event triggers so that my automations continue to start securely.
stories.description: Reuse Falcone HMAC webhook validation and structural tenant/workspace event routing.
requirements: The system must authenticate webhook triggers with rotation-aware signatures, replay protection and size limits.
The system must derive tenant and workspace from verified trigger registration rather than caller-supplied payload fields.
acceptance: Invalid signature, expired replay window and oversized request are rejected before admission.
Foreign workspace identifiers cannot reroute an event.
Publish/update/delete registration reconciliation has no unbounded stale listeners.

stories.title: Implement correlated signals and event waits
stories.story: As a workflow author, I want durable external signals so that workflows can wait without active threads.
stories.description: Persist ordered signal inboxes, bounded early-arrival buffers and explicit correlation policies.
requirements: The system must persist authorized signals using deduplication IDs and explicit run/node-occurrence correlation.
The system must define TTL, capacity and terminal-run behavior for unmatched or early-arriving signals.
acceptance: Signal-before-wait survives restart and is consumed by its intended occurrence.
Duplicate and unauthorized signals do not unblock additional nodes.
Overflow and stale signals produce documented errors/dead-letter records without tenant data leakage.

categories.name: Human approvals and compensation
categories.goal: Extend Falcone business workflows with auditable decisions and recoverable cleanup.

stories.title: Preserve human approval behavior
stories.story: As a reviewer, I want authorized approval decisions so that sensitive steps need accountable consent.
stories.description: Preserve existing flowApproval/human-approval semantics at the facade while binding decisions to authenticated actors.
requirements: The system must derive approval actor identity from verified authentication and enforce configured reviewer permissions.
The system must preserve approval outcome fields and distinguish rejection, timeout and cancellation.
acceptance: Forged actor fields are ignored or rejected; an unauthorized reviewer cannot decide.
Concurrent approval submissions produce one accepted decision and auditable conflicts.
Legacy untargeted approval behavior is explicitly fixture-tested; stricter occurrence targeting uses a versioned change.

stories.title: Add versioned saga compensation
stories.story: As a business process owner, I want compensating actions so that partial success can be repaired.
stories.description: Add an opt-in DSL extension for compensation, leaving v1.0 behavior intact.
requirements: The system must record completed compensatable operations and schedule configured compensations in dependency-safe reverse order.
The system must track compensation retries, failures and manual intervention separately from the original task outcome.
acceptance: A failed later task compensates only committed successful predecessors.
A crash during compensation resumes without skipping or blindly duplicating completed cleanup.
UI/API distinguish failed, compensating, compensated and compensation-failed without rewriting history.

stories.title: Provide audited operator repair actions
stories.story: As an authorized operator, I want controlled repair tools so that ambiguous outcomes can be resolved safely.
stories.description: Support retry-from-known-boundary and reconciliation acknowledgements; disallow arbitrary history edits.
requirements: The system must require authorization, reason and expected run revision for manual repair or retry actions.
The system must preserve original history and create explicit linked attempts or continuation records for repair.
acceptance: Stale revision or cross-tenant repair requests fail before mutation.
Preview identifies side effects that may repeat and requires a documented resolution for ambiguous tasks.
Every accepted repair records actor, reason, prior revision and resulting attempt lineage.

categories.name: Security, tenancy and Falcone quotas
categories.goal: Keep identity, policy and resource accounting under Falcone ownership.

stories.title: Preserve tenant and workspace authorization
stories.story: As a tenant administrator, I want strict isolation so that no other tenant can observe or operate my workflows.
stories.description: Use verified Keycloak/Falcone identity, deny-by-default engine authorization, PostgreSQL RLS and explicit workspace binding.
requirements: The system must enforce tenant/workspace ownership for definitions, runs, events, schedules, payloads and monitoring streams using verified identity.
The system must preserve Falcone definition-write role restrictions and test authorization on every execution lifecycle operation.
acceptance: Cross-tenant and cross-workspace negative tests cover API, worker completion, SSE and object references.
RLS is enforced for application-role queries and pooled connections cannot retain prior tenant context.
Production trusts only authenticated gateway/service identities; injected headers or body tenant IDs cannot elevate access.

stories.title: Replace Temporal-bound credentials safely
stories.story: As a security engineer, I want native execution credentials so that activities retain least privilege after migration.
stories.description: Replace Temporal ancestry lookup with authoritative native run lineage; use short-lived capabilities and secret references.
requirements: The system must bind execution credential references to authoritative tenant, workspace, root run and allowed child lineage before connector use.
The system must renew or reauthorize long-lived runs under Falcone policy without storing bearer tokens or secret values in history.
acceptance: Foreign, expired, revoked and sibling-run references fail closed.
Children and retries inherit only declared scope using recorded lineage, never caller-provided ancestry.
History/log scans contain no raw execution tokens; credential-store outage produces a bounded retryable failure.

stories.title: Implement fair admission and quota accounting
stories.story: As a Falcone operator, I want centrally managed limits so that retries and noisy tenants cannot exhaust capacity.
stories.description: Separate stored definitions, waiting runs, runnable steps, external activities and message rate; integrate Falcone policy and billing ledgers.
requirements: The system must consume versioned Falcone quota policy for starts, active tasks, waiting runs, retries, fan-out, payload bytes and retention.
The system must enforce fair tenant/workspace admission with idempotent reservations, releases and usage events across crashes.
acceptance: Concurrent admissions cannot exceed a configured hard limit; expired reservations are reconciled.
A saturated tenant does not starve eligible work from other tenants in the benchmark.
Billing fixtures classify retries, failures, waits and cancellations explicitly; workflow does not invent independent tariff rules.

categories.name: Falcone services and serverless integration
categories.goal: Port first-party adapters and define the boundary with falcone-serverless.

stories.title: Port the existing first-party task catalog
stories.story: As a Falcone developer, I want current task types to work so that workflows remain useful on day one.
stories.description: Extract engine-neutral activity context for DB, storage, functions, events, HTTP, email and LLM tasks.
requirements: The system must preserve qualified contracts for db.query, storage.get/put, functions.invoke, events.publish, http.request, email.send, llm.complete, llm.batch and largeTask.run.
The system must enforce per-connector timeout, payload, credential, egress and workspace policies before performing external calls.
acceptance: Each task type has success/error/cancellation/duplicate-attempt fixtures and an explicit migration status.
HTTP SSRF tests cover redirects, DNS resolution, private/metadata targets and credential forwarding.
External effects run against controlled test services; existing mocks are never reported as live qualification.

stories.title: Define the serverless invocation and checkpoint contract
stories.story: As a platform developer, I want one shared invocation contract so that workflow and serverless can evolve independently.
stories.description: Keep workflow state in falcone-workflow and untrusted computation in falcone-serverless; separate legacy largeTask support.
requirements: The system must define versioned start/status/cancel/result callbacks with stable operation keys, authenticated correlation and explicit cancellation outcomes.
The system must avoid a runtime dependency cycle: falcone-serverless execution primitives must run without calling Temporal or requiring falcone-workflow to execute themselves.
acceptance: A contract simulator tests submit acknowledgement loss, duplicate completion, stale cancellation and checkpoint references.
An ADR records ownership of execution leases, logical retries, metering and checkpoint retention.
Legacy largeTask profiles incompatible with restricted Wasm execution are flagged; no silent native-container fallback is permitted.

stories.title: Preserve asynchronous batch and object-storage behavior
stories.story: As a workflow user, I want large inputs and provider jobs to remain durable so that orchestration is not tied to one process.
stories.description: Use a provider-neutral Falcone S3 interface and submit/status/collect/cancel phases for asynchronous integrations.
requirements: The system must store large payloads through tenant-scoped Falcone object references with content hashes, retention metadata and authorization checks.
The system must persist provider job IDs and bounded poll schedules for batch tasks, including cancellation cleanup and credential expiry.
acceptance: An interrupted LLM batch resumes polling the same provider job; ambiguous submit is reconciled.
Missing or hash-mismatched objects fail explicitly; no cross-tenant object can be dereferenced.
SeaweedFS or another configured S3 provider passes the adapter contract before deployment; backend identity is recorded.

categories.name: Monitoring, audit and performance
categories.goal: Preserve the Falcone run view and make recovery measurable.

stories.title: Implement run history and resumable SSE
stories.story: As a Falcone user, I want the existing run timeline so that I can inspect progress after migration.
stories.description: Project durable native events to existing node-status/log-line/stream-end frames; retain run/node mapping.
requirements: The system must expose ordered tenant-scoped history and compatible SSE frames with stable resumable event cursors.
The system must emit audit events for lifecycle, authorization-sensitive changes, approvals, repair and backend handover.
acceptance: Disconnect/reconnect with Last-Event-ID produces no missing persisted events within retention.
Terminal streams replay retained history and end; expired cursors receive an explicit resynchronization response.
Slow consumers are bounded and cannot block workflow commits or leak foreign run data.

stories.title: Add operational metrics and tracing
stories.story: As an SRE, I want queue and recovery visibility so that failures are detected before workflows stall.
stories.description: Instrument engine transactions, timers, outbox, adapters and leases with OpenTelemetry and Prometheus-compatible metrics.
requirements: The system must measure admission latency, transition throughput, queue age, timer lag, lease expiry, retry rate, outbox lag and database contention.
The system must propagate trace correlation across Falcone services while redacting secrets and controlling metric cardinality.
acceptance: Dashboards separate starts, transitions, messages, running activities and waiting runs.
An injected database outage, broker outage and stalled adapter trigger distinct actionable alerts.
Per-run IDs appear in traces/logs rather than unbounded metric labels; payload logging is redacted.

stories.title: Qualify performance and reliability targets
stories.story: As a product owner, I want measured capacity so that commitments match infrastructure.
stories.description: Publish reproducible load, soak and fault-injection profiles; treat numerical targets as provisional until tested.
requirements: The project must benchmark workflow starts, step transitions, durable waits and activity concurrency independently from Falcone's WebSocket message rate.
The project must publish achieved availability, latency and recovery results against an agreed workload and resource budget before production cutover.
acceptance: Run small/medium/load profiles with 20 tenants, mixed waits and fan-out; publish hardware, DB configuration and percentiles.
Measure p95 start acknowledgement, ready-task dispatch and due-timer lag under load and failure recovery.
Document saturation, fairness and storage growth; do not interpret 100k messages/s as 100k workflow starts/s.

categories.name: Deployment, CI/CD and operations
categories.goal: Operate as a restricted Falcone service without administrator-installed runtimes.

stories.title: Package restricted Kubernetes and OpenShift deployment
stories.story: As a platform operator, I want ordinary namespaced deployment so that restricted clusters can host the engine.
stories.description: Provide containers, Helm manifests, migrations, health probes and documented external service requirements.
requirements: The system must deploy using existing PostgreSQL and standard namespaced resources without mandatory CRDs, operators, cluster roles or privileged containers.
The system must run as non-root with arbitrary allowed UID, read-only root filesystem, dropped capabilities and no host access.
acceptance: Install in a restricted namespace with no permission to create cluster-scoped resources.
Document pre-provisioned namespace, RBAC, DB, gateway and network prerequisites and pass readiness checks.
Test the agreed Kubernetes minors and actual corporate OpenShift version; unsupported versions fail qualification rather than being assumed.

stories.title: Implement upgrade, backup and recovery runbooks
stories.story: As an on-call engineer, I want tested operating procedures so that releases and incidents are recoverable.
stories.description: Use expand/contract schema migrations, drain behavior, PostgreSQL HA and coordinated payload backup policies.
requirements: The system must support rolling compatible upgrades, bounded graceful drain and documented rollback limits for schema and interpreter changes.
The project must provide tested runbooks for database failover, backup restore, stuck runs, queue overload and key rotation.
acceptance: Old/new binaries coexist through a schema expansion and drain test.
A DB failover test fences old owners before new dispatch resumes.
A restore rehearsal reports measured RPO/RTO, required object versions and credential recovery dependencies.

stories.title: Establish CI, security qualification and ownership
stories.story: As a maintainer, I want enforceable release gates so that durability regressions cannot ship unnoticed.
stories.description: Add contract suites, concurrency/fault tests, supply-chain checks and named ownership responsibilities.
requirements: The project must gate releases on contract, isolation, state-machine fault, schema-migration and dependency-security checks.
The project must assign accountable runtime maintenance, SRE on-call, security review and Falcone product ownership before production release.
acceptance: CI checks generated backlog integrity and runs a real PostgreSQL integration suite once implementation exists.
Images have pinned dependencies, SBOMs and signed release artifacts; copied upstream code has documented provenance.
An ownership/runbook review names escalation and patch responsibilities; documentation alone cannot mark runtime qualified.

categories.name: Temporal migration and retirement
categories.goal: Retire Temporal only when Falcone contract and recovery evidence support it.

stories.title: Build a migration inventory and differential harness
stories.story: As a release engineer, I want evidence of semantic parity so that unsupported flows are not cut over.
stories.description: Inventory deployed DSLs, open runs, schedules, Temporal patches and SDK usage; use isolated effects for comparisons.
requirements: The project must inventory Temporal-dependent code, active workflow versions, open executions, schedule ownership and task adapters before selecting migration cohorts.
The project must compare native and Temporal outcomes using deterministic fixtures or isolated effect simulators without doubling production effects.
acceptance: Cover sequence, parallel, branches, approval/cancel races, children, batch polling, retries and schedule errors.
Track each incompatible semantic with owner and resolution; do not copy Temporal history into native tables.
Record the actual deployed image/source baseline separately from repository inspection.

stories.title: Implement staged routing and in-flight drainage
stories.story: As an operator, I want controlled rollout so that existing workflows finish safely.
stories.description: Route new runs by cohort; keep a durable backend locator; drain old runs and retain old worker versions.
requirements: The system must route new starts by approved cohort and persist backend ownership for all later run operations.
The system must keep in-flight Temporal runs on Temporal unless an explicit application-level checkpoint transfer is validated.
acceptance: Rollback routes future starts back while native runs retain native ownership.
Schedule/webhook/event ownership is coordinated to avoid duplicate admission during rollout.
A long-lived Temporal run remains operable until completion or an approved explicit intervention; no automatic restart repeats effects.

stories.title: Qualify retirement and synchronize Falcone documentation
stories.story: As the Falcone owner, I want a verifiable retirement gate so that Temporal can be removed safely.
stories.description: Update Falcone code/charts and the serverless design only after contract readiness; preserve audit/retention obligations.
requirements: The project must verify no remaining required Temporal runs, schedules, credentials or callers before removing the Temporal deployment and SDK dependencies.
The project must update Falcone integration documentation and falcone-serverless workflow references to the native contract with a rollback and retention plan.
acceptance: Scan code, manifests and runtime telemetry for remaining callers and record authorized exceptions.
Complete a no-Temporal end-to-end workflow run covering function invocation, storage, approval and recovery.
Retain required old histories and recovery material, then remove resources only through a separately authorized rollout.
